items.t: Prosus stock faces tougher test as buyback pace slows
sum: Bank of America has added a sharper operating test to the investment case for Prosus. In an analysis published by Finimize on Thursday, November 5, the bank said repurchases have helped contain the holding company's discount to its listed assets, while a slower pace puts more emphasis on portfolio performance.

The latest analysis adds scale to the capital-return story. Bank of America estimates that Prosus has bought back about 30.4 percent of its outstanding shares since June 2022, while parent Naspers has repurchased about 27.8 percent of its own shares. Combined buybacks have reached 49.6 billion US dollars, according to the analysis.

The support is not static. Prosus repurchased about 90 million US dollars of shares in the week from October 26 to October 30, below the roughly 157 million US dollars weekly average since the programme began. If the pace weakens further, the discount will depend more heavily on whether the underlying portfolio delivers stronger growth and profitability.

Bank of America points to Just Eat Takeaway.com and iFood as the key operating areas. Progress at the food-delivery businesses could give investors a second route to a narrower discount, alongside continued share repurchases. The next first-half fiscal update therefore matters not only for earnings, but also for the credibility of Prosus's capital-allocation strategy.

The real-time quote of Prosus stock was 37.61 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 17:44 CET on Friday, November 6, 2026, 0.16 percent above the Xetra close of Friday, November 6, 2026. The comparison uses the Xetra close at 17:35 CET, while the Lang & Schwarz quote was recorded nine minutes later.
The Dutch market backdrop remains relevant as investors follow developments around the AEX.

AEX closes at 1,129.22 points as chip selloff weighs on Amsterdam
sum: The AEX ended Thursday, November 5, 2026, at 1,129.22 points, down 0.62% from Wednesday's close of 1,136.29. The decline came as technology and semiconductor stocks weakened sharply across Europe and on Wall Street. The closing level and daily performance were reported by Reuters via Investing.com.

Technology was the main source of pressure. ASML fell 6.55%, ASM International lost 6.99% and BE Semiconductor Industries dropped 7.30%, according to the closing market report. The weakness followed a broad selloff in semiconductor shares, as investors reassessed the pace and durability of artificial intelligence infrastructure spending. Concerns about the effect of the US midterm-election outcome on data-centre construction and AI investment added to the sector's pressure.

The move in Amsterdam also reflected a much weaker US technology market during the European close. The Nasdaq was reported to be deep in the red, while semiconductor stocks were hit particularly hard after recent earnings and outlook statements renewed questions about demand and valuation. The AEX's technology exposure made the Dutch benchmark more vulnerable to that shift in sentiment.

Several large constituents moved against the market trend. DSM-Firmenich rose 5.49% to 113.30 euros and was the strongest AEX performer. The company benefited after UBS raised its price target following its recent quarterly results. Adyen advanced 4.51% to 892.50 euros, while Prosus gained 2.77% to 38.02 euros.

Market breadth remained negative: 55 Amsterdam-listed stocks fell, compared with 36 gainers, while 13 were unchanged. The pattern indicates that the decline was broad rather than limited to a single index heavyweight, even though the semiconductor complex accounted for much of the AEX's headline weakness.

Thursday's session leaves the Dutch benchmark exposed to developments in global technology shares and to fresh evidence about the returns expected from AI-related capital expenditure. A rotation toward more traditional sectors offered some protection, but the performance gap between chipmakers and selected defensive or consumer-oriented companies remained pronounced. The next session will show whether the selloff stabilizes or continues to dominate European equity trading.

Prosus stock repurchases 2,364,509 shares for EUR 80.9 million
sum: Prosus announced on Tuesday, November 3, that it had repurchased 2,364,509 of its own shares between Monday, October 26, and Friday, October 30. The technology investment group paid an average of EUR 34.2247 per share, bringing the total consideration to EUR 80,924,618.77, or USD 90,291,157.01, according to the company's regulatory announcement.

The purchases form part of the open-ended repurchase programme announced on June 27, 2022. The programme covers ordinary Prosus shares and N ordinary shares in Naspers held by the respective groups' free-float shareholders.

Prosus did not announce a new end date or a change to the programme's framework in the November 3 update. The disclosure instead reports the volume and price of the latest completed buying period, giving shareholders a current view of capital deployed under the existing plan.

For investors, the announcement is relevant because the company continues to use capital for share repurchases while also investing across its technology ecosystem. The latest purchase price provides a reference for the company's buyback activity, but the announcement does not state that the repurchases were made to support the market price or identify a direct effect on earnings per share.

Prosus stock traded at EUR 36.03 on Lang & Schwarz at 11:30:26 CET on Wednesday, November 4, 2026. The real-time quote of Prosus stock gives investors the latest intraday reference for the Amsterdam-listed company.
European equities and the wider regional backdrop are covered in the latest market reports.

items.t: Prosus stock sharpens India strategy with Navi investment
sum: Prosus is sharpening its investment focus in India, where the technology investor wants to add more platform and marketplace businesses across financial services and consumer markets. Ashutosh Sharma, Prosus's India head, outlined the strategy in an interview with Mint reported by TradingView on Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

Prosus recently invested 100 million US dollars in Navi, an Indian fintech platform founded by Flipkart co-founder Sachin Bansal. The Competition Commission of India approved the investment last week, giving Prosus an 8.5 percent stake. The deal is an entirely primary investment and values Navi at more than 13,000 crore rupees.

Sharma said the transaction fills a gap in Prosus's portfolio. PayU, which Prosus owns outright, is focused largely on business-to-business payments and credit, while Navi serves consumers through a single platform spanning UPI payments, credit, insurance and broking.

Navi's operating revenue rose 16.2 percent year on year to 2,981.7 crore rupees in the financial year ended March 31, 2026, according to Tracxn data cited in the report. The company recorded a consolidated net loss of 466 crore rupees, compared with a loss of 126.4 crore rupees in the prior financial year. Navi Finserv, its lending arm, had assets under management of 13,138 crore rupees in fiscal 2026 and had increased that figure to more than 23,440 crore rupees by the middle of this year.

For Prosus, the strategic appeal lies in Navi's multi-product model rather than a single financial service. Sharma described the business as a platform with exposure to payments, lending, insurance and brokerage, giving the investor a broader route into India's consumer economy.

Prosus said it prefers companies that operate as platforms or marketplaces. The group cited investments or holdings including Swiggy, Meesho, Rapido, Urban Company and Ixigo as examples of that approach, alongside PayU and Navi in financial services.

The company is also prepared to hold concentrated positions for an extended period. Sharma pointed to Rapido as one example: Prosus first invested 180 million US dollars in the mobility platform in April 2022, when it was valued at 1.1 billion US dollars.

US Indexes Dip As Tech Earnings Disappoint, European Stocks Rally
sum: US indexes dipped as AI and semiconductor stocks sold off after major technology companies reported disappointing earnings, amid broader concerns about AI spending and profitability.

Concern over the AI trade remains the dominant cross-market theme, after disappointing technology earnings intensified Friday’s US selloff, stockbroking and portfolio management subsidiary of First National Bank (FNB) said in a brief on Monday.

According to market reports, the NASDAQ ended 2.86% lower last week, while the S&P 500 lost 1.82% and the Dow Jones fell 1.09%. Market analysts said US futures are firmer ahead of major earnings, the jobs report, ISM surveys, and the mid-term elections.
Europe proved more resilient despite sovereign debt sustainability concerns, with the FTSE 100 ending the week up 0.07%, while the Euro Stoxx 50 declined 1.22%.
In Asia on Monday, technology shares are supporting Hong Kong, where the Hang Seng Index is trading 0.61% higher, although weak Chinese PMI readings and AI valuation concerns are tempering sentiment.

The Nikkei 225 is up 0.44%. Australia’s ASX 200 closed down 0.58%, as weakness in technology, mining and healthcare outweighed stronger banks ahead of Tuesday’s expected Reserve Bank of Australia rate increase.

In South Africa, the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) is set for a firmer open this morning, with positive global futures and a broad recovery across most Asian markets setting the stage for a rebound after the All Share and Top 40 closed lower.

Prosus stock heads into key week for 0.28-euro distribution
sum: Prosus has set two important trading dates for shareholders in the coming week. According to the Prosus announcement published on October 29, Thursday, November 5, is the last day for N shareholders to trade on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange and appear in the register for the distribution. Friday, November 6, is the last trading day on Euronext Amsterdam for the same purpose.

Prosus has set a gross distribution of 0.28 euros per N share for the year ended March 31, 2026. The default form is a capital repayment, while eligible holders can elect to receive a dividend instead. The choice matters for the tax treatment and timing of the proceeds.

The JSE ex-dividend and capital repayment date is November 6. On Euronext Amsterdam, the ex-dividend date follows on Monday, November 9, while the record date is Tuesday, November 10. Prosus says transfers of N ordinary shares between the JSE and Euronext Amsterdam will not be permitted from November 6 through November 10 because of the differing ex-dividend dates.

The dividend or capital repayment election period for N shares runs from Wednesday, November 11, through Wednesday, November 25. The payment date is set for Thursday, December 3. Investors choosing the dividend option should also consider the applicable withholding taxes and their own tax residence before making an election.

Prosus stock: Fair Value Calculator values Prosus stock at EUR 51.70
sum: Prosus is valued at EUR 51.70 per share by Fair Value Calculator as of October 20, 2026, compared with the latest euro market quotation of EUR 34.57. The model-based estimate comes from 21 valuation models and is not an analyst target, according to Fair Value Calculator. Prosus was last at EUR 34.57 on Euronext Amsterdam on October 21, 2026 at 5:18 p.m. CEST, up 0.14 percent versus the Xetra close of EUR 34.52.

The valuation page puts fair value EUR 17.13 above the market quotation, a difference of 49.55 percent relative to the market price. Its calculation uses audited fiscal 2026 figures and combines discounted cash flow, earnings, asset-based and dividend models, rather than following one research firm's target.

The same analysis reports a price-to-earnings ratio of 7.50 as of October 16, 2026 and a dividend yield of 0.80 percent. It also gives a cautious scenario of EUR 33.88 and an optimistic scenario of EUR 80.73, showing how strongly the result depends on the assumptions used.

Prosus had a EUR 72.2 billion market capitalization on October 21, 2026. The 52-week range was EUR 34.38 to EUR 63.94, putting the last quotation EUR 0.19, or 0.30 percent, above the low and 45.93 percent below the high. Trading volume reached 2,319,508 shares in the same market snapshot.

That price position gives the valuation gap a concrete market context. The lower end of the Fair Value Calculator scenario range is EUR 33.88, only EUR 0.69 below the latest quotation, while the base estimate is materially higher at EUR 51.70.

Prosus reported on October 20, 2026 that it had repurchased 2,303,676 Prosus shares between October 12 and October 16. The average repurchase price was EUR 35.9303 per share, and the total consideration was EUR 82,771,800.60, according to the company's Prosus release dated October 20, 2026.

The transaction shows the scale of the ongoing buyback program without changing the separate valuation question. For shareholders, the key contrast is between a EUR 51.70 model estimate and a quotation near the EUR 34.38 52-week low.

sum: Prosus has scheduled its next results for November 25, 2026, according to Yahoo Finance. The date gives investors a defined checkpoint after a fiscal year in which the group reported stronger ecosystem growth. At Lang & Schwarz, Prosus was trading at EUR 35.40 on October 20, 2026 at 3:12 p.m. CEST, down 0.84 percent versus the Xetra close of October 19, 2026 at EUR 35.70.

S&P Global Ratings reported that Prosus ecosystem revenue increased 12.00 percent at constant exchange rates and excluding acquisitions in fiscal year 2026. Adjusted EBITDA reached USD 839.00 million, compared with USD 484.00 million in fiscal year 2025. The comparison points to a material improvement in operating earnings, but the figures include the rating agency's adjusted presentation.

The EUR 35.40 quote was EUR 0.92 above Prosus's 52-week low of EUR 34.48 and 44.64 percent below its 52-week high of EUR 63.94, with both levels dated October 20, 2026. The price was accompanied by a volume of 751,108 shares at 3:04 p.m. CEST. The stock's same-day move was modest compared with its yearly range, keeping the price position more important than the daily percentage.

Prosus carried a price-to-earnings multiple of 7.51 and a market capitalization of EUR 74.2 billion as of October 20, 2026. The market value places the holding company close to the lower end of its annual trading range, while the earnings multiple provides a dated valuation reference without establishing a forecast.

On October 7, 2026, S&P Global Ratings revised Prosus's issuer outlook to positive from stable and affirmed its BBB/A-2 ratings. The report said non-Tencent e-commerce dividends rose to USD 463.00 million in fiscal year 2026 from USD 268.00 million in fiscal year 2025. It also identified investment in iFood, Just Eat Takeaway.com and artificial intelligence as factors that could constrain adjusted EBITDA and cash flow in fiscal year 2027.

The next company checkpoint is November 25, 2026, while the October 20 quotation places Prosus 0.84 percent below its Xetra close. That combination gives the market a dated event to watch alongside the current valuation and operating comparison.

Food Delivery Update Might Change The Case For Investing In Prosus Stock (ENXTAM:PRX)
sum: Prosus N.V. recently issued a voluntary business update focused on its Food Delivery segment in a shareholder letter published on its website, with underlying figures not yet audited or reviewed by its independent auditor.
The focus on Food Delivery as a standalone update hints at management attention on this unit's operating profile, business model resilience, and cash demands within the broader Prosus portfolio.
The focus now shifts to how Prosus's Food Delivery business update might influence the wider investment narrative built around ecosystem efficiencies.

Scan how Prosus positions Food Delivery within its broader portfolio, then compare it with a curated group of ecosystem driven platforms in the 618 high quality undiscovered gems that may still be flying under the radar.

To own Prosus, you need to believe its ecosystem model, from Food Delivery to classifieds and fintech, can translate shared data and playbooks into better efficiency and earnings quality over time. The Food Delivery update does not look like a major reset. It reads more as management opening the hood on one of the more capital hungry pieces of the portfolio.

In the near term, the key swing factor is still execution on profitability across e-commerce, especially where one off gains have recently skewed reported net income and margins are lower than last year. The biggest risk is that ecosystem and AI efforts do not translate into cleaner, more repeatable earnings once those unusual items roll off.

The latest Food Delivery letter matters most because it intersects with Prosus’ broader push to extract more from existing assets rather than simply adding new ones using its roughly US$10b cash position. Food platforms sit at the junction of consumer data, logistics and payments, which ties directly into the group’s AI and fraud prevention ambitions.

sum: Our analysts just identified a stock with the potential to be the next Nvidia. Tell us how you invest and we'll show you why it's our #1 pick. Tap here.
Prosus wants investors to stop seeing it mainly as a holding company built around its Tencent stake and start seeing an operating technology group with AI running through the middle.

The latest leadership overhaul creates dedicated AI, technology and product chiefs, giving CEO Fabricio Bloisi a team designed to turn the group's enormous commerce data set into products that can be used across food delivery, fintech, classifieds and online marketplaces.
Prosus shares rose roughly 4% to 6% after the Amsterdam-listed technology group unveiled a new senior leadership structure focused specifically on AI, technology and product development.

Euro Beinat, who has led Prosus's AI and data-science operations since 2018, becomes Chief AI Officer with responsibility for building what the company wants to become a leading European AI laboratory.
Paul van der Boor has been promoted from vice president of AI to Chief Technology Officer, while WeTransfer co-founder Ronald Hans, better known as Nalden, joins as Chief Product Officer.

The appointments create a clearer division of responsibilities inside the group. Beinat will focus on AI models and research, van der Boor on the technology infrastructure needed to deploy those systems across the portfolio, and Hans on turning them into products that customers and merchants might actually use.

sum: The board of directors ("Board") has decided to nominate Pedro Arnt (53) as an independent non-executive director to the Prosus Board, as well as a member of the audit and risk committees, at a specially to be scheduled general meeting of the company.

With effect from 10 August 2026, Mr Arnt has been appointed as an independent non-executive director of Naspers Limited. Mr Arnt has been classified as an independent non-executive director of Naspers under the King Report V on Corporate Governance for South Africa, 2025 and Prosus under the Dutch Corporate Governance Code.

Mr Arnt earned a BA in Political Science from Haverford College in 1995 and an MPhil in Latin American Studies from the University of Oxford in 1997. He began his career at The Boston Consulting Group as an Associate, advising Global 500 companies across Latin America and the United States, with a focus on the emerging electronic commerce practice during the internet expansion of the late 1990s. In 1999, Pedro joined MercadoLibre as one of the company’s earliest executives, working across marketing, sales, customer operations, treasury and investor relations. He served as VP of Marketing & Sales, then as VP of Customer Operations from 2003, before being appointed VP of Planning, Treasury & Investor Relations in 2007, playing a key role in the company’s Nasdaq initial public offering that year. In 2011, he was appointed Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer of MercadoLibre, a role he held for more than twelve years, during which the company grew into one of Latin America’s largest technology and fintech platforms, reaching a market capitalisation of approximately US$100 billion. Pedro joined dLocal in August 2023 as Co-Chief Executive Officer, becoming standalone Chief Executive Officer in 2024, a role he holds today. He also serves as a Non-Executive Director of Allegro.eu SA.

The Board confirms that in compliance with the JSE Listings Requirements fit and proper assessments have been conducted and that the Board is satisfied with the outcomes of the assessments. Additionally, the Group confirms that there are no positive statements to report in respect of the integrity information contained in the director’s declarations.

South African billionaire Koos Bekker opens $14,000-a-night lodge in second English village
sum: The Newt in Somerset, the English country estate owned by South African billionaire Koos Bekker and his wife Karen Roos, has opened a 16-bedroom private house that rents from £10,500 a night, about $14,100, extending the couple's footprint into a second Somerset village.

Yarlington Lodge opened on June 1 in the village of Yarlington, roughly a mile from the main estate at Hadspen House. The property sits within 12 acres of restored gardens, woodland and grounds, and completes a multi-year restoration led by Roos with the architecture practice Richard Parr Associates.

The expansion arrives weeks after residents of Castle Cary, the nearby town where Bekker has bought the Creamery Cafe at the railway station, a delicatessen, a beauty parlour, several high street businesses and The George, a 600-year-old pub now closing for refurbishment, launched a campaign urging visitors to boycott his businesses.

The Grade II listed site centres on a Regency rectory and consists of three residences. The main lodge holds eight bedrooms, two of which form a family suite with a shared bathroom. The Coach House, converted from former stables and a carriage store, holds four. Cottage in the Wall, once a gardener's cottage, holds another four. Together they sleep up to 32 guests.

The three buildings share a historic walled garden, formal lawns, an indoor-outdoor swimming pool, a tennis court, a croquet lawn, a cinema room, a speakeasy bar and a glasshouse used for dining. The rate covers exclusive use of all 16 bedrooms and includes a 12-month membership of The Newt from the date of stay.

Each bedroom in the main house is named after a literary character of the Regency period, among them Jane Bennet and Natalya Rostova, with the corresponding novel placed beside the bed. A butler team arranges spa treatments, personal trainers, childcare and nanny services. Guests can cook in fully equipped kitchens or draw on estate chefs working with produce from The Newt's kitchen gardens, butchery, dairy and creamery. The land was granted by Henry VIII to Catherine Parr, his last wife.
Rooms at the main Newt hotel start at £795 a night, roughly $1,070, across 42 bedrooms at Hadspen and the Farmyard accommodation opened in 2020.

Prosus gives irrevocable undertaking to sell residual stake in delivery hero to uber
sum: Prosus N.V. (“Prosus”) announces that it has provided an irrevocable undertaking to Uber Technologies, Inc. (“Uber”) to sell all of its remaining 16.8% stake in Delivery Hero SE (“Delivery Hero”) to Uber upon completion of Uber’s recently announced offer to acquire the share capital in Delivery Hero at a purchase price of €41.50 per ordinary share (the “Offer”). Uber is headquartered in San Francisco, California, United States, and its issued shares are admitted to listing and trading on the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE: UBER), with secondary listings in several stock exchanges across Europe and the Americas.

Under the terms of the European Commission’s approval of the acquisition by Prosus of Just Eat Takeaway.com, Prosus committed to significantly reduce its 26.5% shareholding in Delivery Hero. In compliance with those commitments, on 17 April 2026 Prosus announced the disposal of 13,582,342 ordinary shares it held in Delivery Hero SE to Uber, representing approximately 4.5% of Delivery Hero's issued share capital; and on 11 May 2026, Prosus announced a further disposal of 15,188,284 ordinary shares in Delivery Hero to Aspex Management representing approximately 5% of Delivery Hero's issued share capital.

Prosus now holds a minority stake of 16.8% in Delivery Hero, and Uber holds a stake of 24.99% with a further 11.8% held via instruments. Uber’s Offer represents a significant premium of 151% to Delivery Hero’s 1-month VWAP before the announcement of Prosus’s initial 4.5% stake sale to Uber. Prosus believes that Uber’s offer represents a fair price and effective way to comply with its commitments to the European Commission. Therefore, to support the offer, Prosus has entered into an irrevocable undertaking to Uber to dispose of its remaining interest in Delivery Hero. Prosus intends to use the proceeds of the disposal for general corporate purposes.

The Offer will be subject to, amongst other things, customary regulatory conditions and the Offer then becoming unconditional and proceeding to implementation in accordance with its terms. As such there is no certainty that the Offer will be implemented. The details of the Offer, including the outstanding conditions, are available on Uber’s website: www.uber.com.

UBER Reportedly Eyeing €12.5B Delivery Hero Takeover To Challenge DoorDash
sum: - Sources close to the talks told FT that the final terms and timing have not yet been confirmed and could still change.
- Uber first approached Delivery Hero in May with an initial offer of €33 per share.
- Uber’s rival DoorDash acquired Deliveroo in 2025 to expand its European footprint.
Uber Technologies (UBER) is reportedly preparing to buy German food delivery company Delivery Hero in a deal valued at around €12.5 billion as it seeks to challenge DoorDash in global markets.

The transaction is expected to be announced as early as Thursday, with Uber offering around €41 per share, the Financial Times reported, citing people familiar with the matter. Sources close to the talks told the FT that final terms and timing have not yet been confirmed and could still change.

Delivery Hero reportedly plans to sell its Turkish business, Yemeksepeti, and several European operations to an investment firm to reduce geographic overlap with Uber and lower the risk of competition concerns from regulators. Uber has also paused the launch of delivery services in five new European markets that overlap with Delivery Hero operations, the report noted.

The acquisition would strengthen Uber’s position in the Middle East by adding Talabat and Saudi Arabia’s HungerStation. It would also bring Delivery Hero’s South Korean platform Baemin into Uber’s portfolio, the report added.

items.t: Uber said to be in advanced talks on Delivery Hero takeover
sum: Uber aims to reach an agreement with Delivery Hero as soon as this week
[BERLIN] Ride-hailing giant Uber Technologies is in advanced talks to acquire German food-delivery company Delivery Hero, people familiar with the matter said.

Shares of Delivery Hero have gained about 62 per cent this year, giving the company a market value of 11.2 billion euros (US$12.8 billion). Uber has already built a shareholding in Delivery Hero of 24.99 per cent, plus derivatives that take its total interest to about 36.8 per cent.

Uber has previously approached Delivery Hero with an offer of 33 euros per share, but investors have been betting that a higher price will be required to seal the deal. Amsterdam-listed internet investment firm Prosus NV also holds a significant stake in Delivery Hero.

Any deal is likely to attract scrutiny from antitrust regulators globally. Delivery Hero has a presence in more than 60 markets, and the company and Uber overlap in parts of Europe and the Middle East.

Deliberations are ongoing and a deal could still be delayed or fall apart, the people said, asking not to be identified because the information is private. Representatives for Uber and Prosus declined to comment. A spokesperson for Delivery Hero couldn’t immediately be reached for comment.

Delivery Hero has been conducting a strategic review following pressure from shareholders, which include Aspex Management, the hedge fund that succeeded in ousting founder Niklas Östberg and has lobbied for more asset sales.

Flipkart co-founder Sachin Bansal's Navi plans to launch Rs 3,000 crore IPO by March 2027: Report
sum: Fintech company Navi Ltd, co-founded by Flipkart co-founder Sachin Bansal, is preparing to file draft papers for an IPO by the January-March quarter of FY27, according to an Economic Times report.
The Bengaluru-based company is looking to raise about Rs 3,000 crore through the proposed IPO, the report said.

The issue is expected to include both a fresh sale of shares and an offer for sale, although the final structure has not yet been decided. Kotak Investment Banking is working with Navi on the planned public issue.

The move would mark Navi’s second attempt to list on the stock exchanges. The company filed draft papers for a Rs 3,350 crore IPO in 2022 and received approval from the SEBI later that year, but did not proceed with the issue as market conditions weakened for technology companies.

Before returning to the public markets, Navi is also said to be in talks to raise its first external equity funding round, led by Dutch technology investor Prosus. The proposed fundraise is expected to help set a valuation benchmark ahead of the IPO.
“The valuation is being discussed, and there’s some pushback from Prosus,” a person told ET anonymously.
Prosus is said to be willing to invest at a valuation of about Rs 13,000 crore. The size of the round and the final valuation have not yet been agreed.
